interpretation: Chemicals, pulp, panel, pellet, liquid fuels, and other industrial demands can compete with energy for the same residue. The facility chain assigns process residue by class and province but does not net out internal mill consumption or existing industrial/chemical contracts. If OSeCAN treats those volumes as committed, available energy residue is lower than the handoff total; if OSeCAN adds new chemical or biofuel demand, the same residue may be counted twice. No quantity is assigned here.
recommendation: Report process residue gross and flag industrial/chemical demand as un-netted until the OSeCAN demand stack and mill self-use boundary are supplied. Do not double count the same residue as both industrial feedstock and energy supply.
